description: Ten user-selected region/year research scenarios using officially published allowance budgets, planning constraints, or emissions pathways. These are not a claim of legal compliance or a reproduction of each official planning scenario.
solver_cap_unit: million metric tonnes of direct operational CO2 per representative 8760-hour year

general_mapping.emissions_scope: Direct operational emissions from dispatched existing assets with nonzero inventory emissions factors; lifecycle and external import emissions are excluded.
general_mapping.policy_mode: baseline leaves the independent operational_co2_budget constraint active; published-policy constraints are separate.
general_mapping.feasibility: An input ceiling does not establish that a feasible design exists. Full 8760-hour runs and shorter proportional-budget diagnostics must be distinguished.
general_mapping.input_basis: 2023 uses experiment/<region>; 2030/2035 use weather_prediction/inputs/<year>/<region>, retaining their existing demand, fleet, network and synthetic future weather profiles.

mapping.gas_mapping: CO2 to CO2; convert US short tons to metric tonnes using the exact factor 0.90718474.
mapping.scope_mapping: Use the New York base allowance budget as a strict model-wide annual dispatch ceiling. Model assets and regulated-unit coverage are not identical.

mapping.source_scope: South African electricity-sector CO2 emissions in the IRP 2025 balanced plan.

mapping.gas_mapping: Published MtCO2 is adopted directly as the numerical MtCO2 dispatch ceiling.
mapping.scope_mapping: Research adoption of the balanced-plan emissions trajectory as a model-wide hard annual ceiling.
caveats: The published value is an emissions pathway/output, not a verified legal annual emissions cap.

source.title: Mexico Programa Sectorial de Energía 2025–2030 (PROSENER)
source.locator: Electricity-generation emissions paragraph: net-injected-electricity emissions peak in 2027, then decline 23.9% from 156.42 to 119 MtCO2e by the 2030 planning horizon.

mapping.source_scope: SEN greenhouse-gas emissions associated with net injected electricity.
mapping.model_scope: Nine control regions, including Baja California and Baja California Sur; SIMUL/Mulege excluded.
mapping.gas_mapping: CO2e-to-direct-CO2 numerical proxy: impose the published 119 MtCO2e number as 119 Mt of modelled direct CO2. This is a declared approximation, not a gas conversion or an official CO2-only cap.
mapping.scope_mapping: Use the national net-injected-electricity pathway as a research ceiling for the nine-region model, without proportional rescaling.
caveats: The source is a planned emissions outcome, not a verified legal annual electricity-sector cap.
Demand uses PRODESEN 2024–2038 while the emissions pathway uses PROSENER 2025–2030.
The model excludes 186 GWh of SIMUL/Mulege demand from the published 410800 GWh SEN total for 2030; no emissions allocation to the excluded subsystem is inferred.
Non-CO2 greenhouse gases and emissions from external electricity imports are not separately represented.

source.title: Brazil EPE/MME Plano Decenal de Expansão de Energia 2035, approved final report
source.locator: Table 10-1, p. 393, SIN row, 2030; scope/hydrology discussion pp. 394–395 and explicit absence of model GHG limits p. 396.

mapping.source_scope: Brazil Sistema Interligado Nacional (SIN), excluding isolated systems and separate autoproduction.
mapping.model_scope: Four SIN subsystem load regions N, NE, SE and S; Itaipu Paraguayan-side units placed in SE.
mapping.gas_mapping: CO2e-to-direct-CO2 numerical proxy: impose the published SIN MtCO2e number as the same number of Mt of modelled direct CO2. This is a declared approximation, not a gas conversion or an official CO2-only cap.
mapping.scope_mapping: Use the SIN row, not the whole-electricity-sector totals (59 MtCO2e in 2030 and 62 in 2035).
caveats: PDE 2035 states that the planning model does not impose explicit GHG emissions targets or limits; these projections become constraints only in this research experiment.

Forecasts assume average hydrology; drought can materially increase projected emissions. The model retains the existing 2023-derived hydro-energy assumptions and uses its weather_prediction target-year synthetic solar/wind profiles.
Non-CO2 greenhouse gases and external import emissions are not separately represented.
